title: The Frogs and the Well
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Two Frogs lived together in a marsh. But one hot summer the marsh dried up, and they left it to look for another place to live in: for frogs like damp places if they can get them. By and by they came to a deep well, and one of them looked down into it, and said to the other, "This looks a nice cool place: let us jump in and settle here." But the other, who had a wiser head on his shoulders, replied, "Not so fast, my friend: supposing this well dried up like the marsh, how should we get out again?" Think twice before you act.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the two Frogs live together at first?
According to the passage, why did the Frogs leave the marsh?
options: It dried up in the hot summer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Frogs come to as they searched for a new home?
According to the passage, what does the first Frog suggest they do at the well?
According to the passage, what question does the wiser Frog raise?
options: How deep is the well, really?
Supposing this well dried up like the marsh, how should we get out again?
Are there enough insects to eat down there?
Will the other frogs join them?

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does the phrase "a wiser head on his shoulders" suggest about the second Frog?
options: He was more cautious and thoughtful than the other Frog
He was physically larger than the other Frog
He was older in years than the other Frog
He was less experienced than the other Frog

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the second Frog hesitate to jump into the well?
options: He dislikes the cool temperature of the water
He recognizes that the well could dry up just as the marsh did, trapping them inside
He wants to search for a marsh instead of a well
He is afraid of the depth alone, regardless of water

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable's closing line?
options: Wells are always more dangerous than marshes
One should consider the consequences of a decision before committing to it
Frogs should never leave their home marsh
Cool places are not always as good as they seem

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of places do frogs like, if they can get them?
According to the passage, what did the first Frog say the well looked like?
According to the passage, what word does the second Frog use to address the first Frog?
As the passage uses it, what does "settle" mean in "let us jump in and settle here"?
options: To argue and come to terms

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why would getting out of the well be a problem if it dried up, unlike the open marsh?
options: A well's steep, enclosed sides would trap them where a marsh's open ground would not
The well would fill with mud instead of drying completely
Other frogs would already have taken the marsh by then
The well was farther from other water sources than the marsh had been

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: One Frog wants to settle in a well at once, but the other cautions that they should first think about what would happen if it dried up too
Two Frogs search for a new marsh after their well dries up
Two Frogs argue over which of them found the well first
Two Frogs decide to return to their old marsh instead of the well
